summary: A reply now ends her turn unless she says more is coming, which removes a model call that almost never sent anything; and before long work she can say what she is doing first, then answer.
details: send_reply takes `more` and `heads_up`; without either the turn is over once the message lands.

Before work that will keep the room waiting (a search, the computer, an image), she may send one short line saying what she is doing, marked as a heads-up, then the answer; a quick check still gets no filler.
If her answer after a heads-up comes back as plain text instead of a send, or the turn is cut off, it is still recovered or answered by the fallback.
Multi-message replies still work when she passes `more=true`; the cap stays at three.
limitations: She sends the heads-up rarely: 2 of about 25 long-work eval draws.
A heads-up held for review leaves the answer unsent, since a held send tells her not to send again.
Fire turns (proactive, heartbeat) do not re-open the fallback after a heads-up.
The fallback after a heads-up needs her to mark the line as one; a heads-up sent with only `more` is not caught.
